title: Timeline Construction — Core Method
description: The tracker builds timelines by extracting every dated event from the records — creation, modification, citation, supersession — normalizing the timestamps and sorting them into one chronological spine. Events with uncertain dates carry ranges instead of points, and the timeline shows the uncertainty honestly. Multiple records' events interleave on the same spine, revealing the actual historical sequence. A constructed timeline turns a pile of dated records into a story with an order. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Sequence Alignment — Core Method
description: Two archives often describe the same history with different granularity, and sequence alignment matches their event sequences the way bioinformatics aligns DNA. The alignment scores matches, tolerates gaps, and reports the correspondence between the two timelines. Aligned sequences reveal which archive is more complete and where they contradict. This is the rigorous way to merge histories instead of just stacking them. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
demo:
a = ["start", "v1", "v2"]
b = ["start", "v1", "patch", "v2"]
i = j = 0
while i < len(a) and j < len(b):
    if a[i] == b[j]: print("match:", a[i]); i += 1; j += 1
    else: print("gap in A:", b[j]); j += 1

title: Version Change Detection — Core Method
description: Records evolve across versions, and the tracker diffs successive versions to name exactly what changed, when, and by whom. Changes are classified — correction, addition, retraction, reorganization — because a retraction matters more than a typo fix. The version chain becomes a first-class object the tracker can query: 'show me everything that changed about X in 2021'. Change detection turns version history from storage overhead into knowledge. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
provenance: JAH Databases archive-intelligence tools program, lane T2a — public methods from established computer-science practice.

title: Event Correlation — Core Method
description: Events close in time across different records are often causally linked — a policy change followed by a migration wave — and the tracker correlates them by temporal proximity plus shared entities. Correlation windows are sized to the domain: minutes for system logs, months for policy histories. Each correlation carries a strength from the overlap of entities and the tightness of timing. Temporal correlation proposes hypotheses; it never asserts causation. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
provenance: JAH Databases archive-intelligence tools program, lane T2a — public methods from established computer-science practice.

title: Trend Linking — Core Method
description: Beyond individual events, the tracker links trends: rising citation counts, growing record sizes, accelerating update rates. A trend is a time series with a fitted direction, and linked trends across topics suggest systemic shifts — the whole archive moving toward video, for instance. Trend links are reported with their slopes and confidence, not as vibes. This is how the tracker sees the forest changing, not just the trees. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
demo:
series = [10, 12, 15, 19, 24]
n = len(series)
slope = (n * sum(i * v for i, v in enumerate(series)) - sum(range(n)) * sum(series)) /         (n * sum(i * i for i in range(n)) - sum(range(n)) ** 2)
print("trend slope: %.1f per period -> %s" % (slope, "rising" if slope > 0 else "flat"))
